curriculum: Indian Nursing Council (Revised Regulations and Curriculum for B.Sc. (Nursing) Program) Regulations, 2020 - notified 5 July 2021, in force from 2021-22
credit_rule: 1 theory credit = 20 hours (1 hour/week over a semester)

U75.label: University paper, single subject, 75 marks, 3 hours

U37_38.label: University paper, two sections (37 + 38 = 75 marks), 3 hours

U25_50.label: University paper: Biochemistry 25 + Nutrition 50 = 75 marks, 3 hours

U38_25_12.label: University paper: Pharmacology 38 + Pathology 25 + Genetics 12 = 75 marks, 3 hours

U55_20.label: University paper: Nursing Research 55 + Statistics 20 = 75 marks, 3 hours

C50.label: College end-semester exam, set for 50 marks and scaled to 25

pattern_note: This is the INC model blueprint as adopted by most health-science universities. Universities may add choice (for example 'answer any one of two essays') or split essays into sub-parts (2 + 4 + 4, 2 + 5 + 8 and so on). This question bank covers the descriptive part only (2, 5, 10 and 15 marks); the 1-mark MCQ block is left out on purpose.

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Digestive System Disorders

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Cardiovascular Disorders (including BCLS)
units.topics: Hypertension; arteriosclerosis and peripheral vascular disease; coronary artery disease, angina and myocardial infarction; valvular and rheumatic heart disease; infective endocarditis; dysrhythmias and heart block; heart failure; cardiogenic shock and cardiac tamponade; cardiopulmonary arrest; basic cardiac life support (BCLS) module

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Haematological Disorders
units.topics: Anaemias; polycythaemia; bleeding disorders - haemophilia, ITP, DIC; thalassaemia; leukaemia, leukopenia and agranulocytosis; lymphomas and multiple myeloma

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Endocrine Disorders

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Integumentary Disorders
units.topics: Skin infections and infestations; dermatitis and dermatoses; acne, allergies, eczema, pemphigus; psoriasis; malignant melanoma; alopecia; special and alternative therapies; drugs used in skin disorders

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Musculoskeletal Disorders
units.topics: Dislocation, fracture, sprain, strain, contusion, amputation; osteomyelitis and bone tumours; casts, splints, traction and crutch walking; bursitis, synovitis and arthritis; osteoporosis, osteomalacia and Paget's disease; spinal deformities and disc prolapse; rehabilitation, prostheses and joint replacement

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Communicable Diseases
units.topics: Overview of the infectious process; tuberculosis; diarrhoeal diseases; viral hepatitis A to E; typhoid; herpes, chickenpox, measles, mumps, influenza; meningitis; gas gangrene; leprosy; dengue, malaria, chikungunya, plague, filariasis, swine flu; diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, poliomyelitis; COVID-19; isolation, quarantine and immunisation

units.title: Drugs used in Disorders of Ear, Nose, Throat and Eye
units.topics: Antihistamines; topical applications for the eye (chloramphenicol, gentamicin eye drops), ear (soda glycerine, boric spirit ear drops), nose and buccal cavity (chlorhexidine mouthwash); composition, action, dosage, route, indications, contraindications, drug interactions, side effects and nursing implications

units.title: Drugs used on Urinary System
units.topics: Pharmacology of commonly used drugs: renin–angiotensin system; diuretics and antidiuretics; drugs toxic to the kidney; urinary antiseptics; treatment of UTI – acidifiers and alkalinisers

units.title: Drugs acting on Nervous System
units.topics: Analgesics – NSAIDs, antipyretics, opioids and other central analgesics; general anaesthesia (techniques, pre-anaesthetic medication) and local anaesthetics; medical gases (oxygen, nitrous oxide, carbon dioxide); hypnotics and sedatives; skeletal muscle relaxants; antipsychotics and mood stabilisers; antidepressants; antianxiety drugs; anticonvulsants; drugs for neurodegenerative disorders; CNS stimulants; ethyl alcohol and treatment of methyl alcohol poisoning

units.title: Drugs used for Hormonal Disorders and Supplementation, Contraception and Medical Termination of Pregnancy
units.topics: Oestrogens and progestins; oral contraceptives and hormone replacement therapy; vaginal contraceptives; drugs for infertility and medical termination of pregnancy; uterine stimulants and relaxants (tocolytics)

units.title: Drugs used for Pregnant Women during Antenatal Period, Labour and Postnatal Period
units.topics: Tetanus prophylaxis; iron and vitamin K1 supplementation; oxytocin and misoprostol; ergometrine; methyl prostaglandin F2-alpha; magnesium sulphate; calcium gluconate

units.title: Miscellaneous Drugs
units.topics: Drugs used for de-addiction; drugs used in CPR and emergency (adrenaline, chlorpheniramine, hydrocortisone, dexamethasone); IV fluids and electrolyte replacement; common poisons, drugs used for treatment of poisoning (activated charcoal, ipecac, antidotes, anti-snake venom); vitamins and minerals supplementation; vaccines and sera (Universal Immunization Programme schedule); anticancer drugs – chemotherapeutic drugs commonly used; immunosuppressants and immunostimulants

units.title: Introduction to Drugs used in Alternative Systems of Medicine
units.topics: Ayurveda, Homeopathy, Unani and Siddha – principles and drugs used for common ailments; AYUSH; safety, interactions and the nurse's role

units.title: Fundamental Principles of Prescribing (Mandatory Module)

courses.title: Pathology II and Genetics
courses.paper: Pharmacology, Pathology & Genetics - Section B Pathology (25) + Section C Genetics (12)

units.title: Pathology II – Special Pathology: Pathological Changes in Disease Conditions of Selected Systems
units.topics: Kidney and urinary tract – glomerulonephritis, pyelonephritis, renal calculi, cystitis, renal cell carcinoma, renal failure (acute and chronic); male genital system – cryptorchidism, testicular atrophy, prostatic hyperplasia, carcinoma penis and prostate; female genital system – carcinoma cervix, carcinoma endometrium, uterine fibroids, vesicular mole and choriocarcinoma, ovarian cyst and tumours; breast – fibrocystic changes, fibroadenoma, carcinoma breast; central nervous system – meningitis, encephalitis, stroke, tumours of CNS

units.title: Pathology II – Clinical Pathology: Body Fluids, Urine and Faeces
units.topics: Examination of body cavity fluids – methods of collection and examination of CSF and other body cavity fluids (sputum, wound discharge) for diagnosis and prognosis; analysis of semen – sperm count, motility and morphology and their importance in infertility; urine – physical characteristics, analysis, culture and sensitivity; faeces – characteristics, stool examination for occult blood, ova, parasites and cysts, reducing substances; methods and collection of urine and faeces for various tests

units.title: Genetics I – Introduction: Nature, Principles and Perspectives of Heredity
units.topics: Application of human genetics in nursing; impact of genetic condition on families; review of cell division – mitosis and meiosis; characteristics and structure of genes; chromosomes – sex determination; chromosomal aberrations; patterns of inheritance – Mendelian theory, multiple allelism and blood groups, sex-linked inheritance; mechanism of inheritance; errors in transmission (mutation)

units.title: Genetics II – Maternal, Prenatal and Genetic Influences on Development of Defects and Diseases
units.topics: Conditions affecting the mother – genetic and infections; consanguinity, atopy; prenatal nutrition and food allergies; maternal age; maternal drug therapy; prenatal testing and diagnosis; effect of radiation, drugs and chemicals; infertility; spontaneous abortion; neural tube defects and the role of folic acid in lowering the risks; Down syndrome (trisomy 21)

units.title: Genetics III – Genetic Testing in the Neonates and Children
units.topics: Screening for congenital abnormalities, developmental delay and dysmorphism; newborn screening for inborn errors and other genetic conditions

units.title: Genetics IV – Genetic Conditions of Adolescents and Adults
units.topics: Cancer genetics – familial cancer; inborn errors of metabolism; blood group alleles and haematological disorders; genetic haemochromatosis; Huntington's disease; mental illness

units.title: Genetics V – Services related to Genetics
units.topics: Genetic testing; gene therapy; genetic counselling; legal and ethical issues; role of the nurse

courses.title: Adult Health Nursing II with integrated pathophysiology including Geriatric Nursing (and Palliative Care module)

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Disorders of Ear, Nose and Throat
units.topics: Review of anatomy and physiology of ear, nose and throat; history, physical assessment and diagnostic tests; external ear – deformities, otalgia, foreign bodies, tumours; middle ear – impacted wax, tympanic membrane perforation, otitis media, mastoiditis, otosclerosis, tumours; inner ear – Meniere's disease, labyrinthitis, ototoxicity, tumours; upper respiratory airway infections – rhinitis, sinusitis, tonsillitis, laryngitis; epistaxis, nasal obstruction, laryngeal obstruction, cancer of oral cavity and larynx; deafness and its management, hearing aids

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Disorders of Eye
units.topics: Review of anatomy and physiology of the eye; history, physical and diagnostic assessment; refractive errors; eyelids – infection and deformities; conjunctiva – inflammation, infection, bleeding; cornea – inflammation and infection; lens – cataract; glaucoma; retinal detachment; blindness; eye donation, eye banking and corneal transplantation

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Kidney and Urinary Problems
units.topics: Review of anatomy and physiology of the genitourinary system; history, physical assessment and diagnostic tests; urinary tract infections – acute, chronic, lower, upper; nephritis, nephrotic syndrome; renal calculi; acute and chronic renal failure (AKI, CKD), dialysis and renal transplantation; disorders of ureter, urinary bladder and urethra; disorders of prostate – inflammation, infection, stricture, obstruction and benign prostatic hypertrophy

units.title: Nursing Management of Disorders of Male Reproductive System
units.topics: Review of anatomy and physiology of the male reproductive system; history, physical assessment and diagnostic tests; infections of testis, penis and adjacent structures – phimosis, epididymitis, orchitis; hydrocele, varicocele, testicular torsion, hypospadias and epispadias; sexual dysfunction, infertility, contraception; male breast disorders – gynaecomastia, tumour, climacteric changes

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Burns, Reconstructive and Cosmetic Surgery
units.topics: Review of anatomy and physiology of skin and connective tissues; history, physical assessment, assessment of burns and fluid and electrolyte loss; burns; reconstructive and cosmetic surgery for burns, congenital deformities, injuries and cosmetic purposes, gender reassignment; legal and ethical aspects; special therapies – vacuum-assisted dressing, laser, liposuction, skin rejuvenation, dermal fillers

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Neurological Disorders
units.topics: Review of anatomy and physiology of the nervous system; history, physical and neurological assessment, diagnostic tests; headache; head injuries; spinal injuries – paraplegia, hemiplegia, quadriplegia; spinal cord compression – herniation of intervertebral disc; intracranial and cerebral aneurysms; meningitis, encephalitis, brain abscess, neurocysticercosis; movement disorders – chorea; seizures and epilepsies; cerebrovascular accident; cranial and spinal neuropathies – Bell's palsy, trigeminal neuralgia; peripheral neuropathies; degenerative diseases – Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease; Guillain–Barré syndrome, myasthenia gravis, multiple sclerosis; brain tumours; rehabilitation of patients with neurological deficit

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Immunological Problems
units.topics: Review of the immune system; nursing assessment – history and physical assessment; HIV and AIDS – epidemiology, transmission, prevention of transmission and management; opportunistic infections; role of the nurse – counselling, health education, home care and rehabilitation; National AIDS Control Programme (NACO) and other national and international agencies

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients with Oncological Conditions (including Palliative Care Module)
units.topics: Structure and characteristics of normal and cancer cells; history, physical assessment, diagnostic tests; prevention, screening, early detection, warning signs of cancer; epidemiology, aetiology, classification, pathophysiology, staging, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, treatment modalities and nursing management; common malignancies – eye, ear, nose, larynx, breast, cervix, ovary, uterus, sarcoma, kidney, bladder, prostate, brain, spinal cord; oncological emergencies; modalities of treatment – chemotherapy, radiotherapy (radiation safety, AERB regulations), surgery, stem cell and bone marrow transplant, immunotherapy, gene therapy; psychological aspects of cancer; supportive care; hospice care; palliative care – principles, symptom management, pain, end-of-life care, alternative therapies

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients in Emergency and Disaster Situations
units.topics: Disaster nursing – concept, principles and related policies; types of disaster – natural and man-made; disaster preparedness – team, guidelines, protocols, equipment, resources; triage; medical and surgical emergencies – polytrauma, bites and stings, poisoning, thermal emergencies (heat stroke, hypothermia, frostbite), drowning; principles of emergency management; emergency drugs; medicolegal aspects

units.title: Nursing Care of the Elderly
units.topics: Nursing assessment – history and physical assessment; ageing – demography, myths and realities, theories of ageing; age-related body system changes; cognitive and psychosocial aspects of ageing; medications and the elderly; stress and coping in older adults; common health problems and nursing management; psychosocial and sexual abuse of the elderly; role of nurse in care of elderly and their caregivers; use of aids and prostheses (hearing aids, dentures); legal and ethical issues; provisions, programmes and privileges for the elderly; home and institutional care

units.title: Nursing Management of Patients in Critical Care Units
units.topics: Principles of critical care nursing; organisation – physical set-up, policies, staffing norms; protocols, equipment and supplies; critical care biomedical equipment – ventilators, cardiac monitors, defibrillators, infusion pumps, resuscitation equipment; mechanical ventilation and its complications; advanced cardiac life support; nursing management of the critically ill patient; transitional care; ethical and legal aspects; breaking bad news – communication with patient and family; end-of-life care

units.title: Nursing Management of Adults including Elderly with Occupational and Industrial Disorders
units.topics: History, physical examination, diagnostic tests; occupational diseases – pneumoconioses (silicosis, asbestosis, coal workers' lung, byssosis), occupational dermatoses, noise-induced hearing loss, lead and other poisoning, occupational cancers; prevention, control and management; occupational health services and legislation

courses.title: Professionalism, Professional Values and Ethics including Bioethics

units.title: Professionalism
units.topics: Profession – definition, characteristics; nursing as a profession; professionalism – definition and characteristics, attributes (accountability, competence, commitment, integrity, collaboration), challenges of professionalism; personal identity versus professional identity; preservation of self-integrity; professional conduct – following rules, policies, code of conduct, dress code; professional etiquette and behaviours; professional boundaries; social media use; professional socialisation; role of nurse in maintaining professionalism

units.title: Professional Values
units.topics: Values – definition, characteristics, types; value clarification and value formation; personal and professional values; core professional values – human dignity, integrity, altruism, autonomy, social justice, caring, confidentiality, accountability; ICN and INC codes; professional values in transcultural care; advocacy – patient advocacy; developing and strengthening professional values

units.title: Ethics and Bioethics
units.topics: Ethics and morality – definitions, ethical theories; ethical principles – autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice, veracity, fidelity, confidentiality; bioethics – definition, scope; ethical issues and dilemmas in nursing; ethical decision-making models; code of ethics and code of professional conduct (INC, ICN); patient rights and responsibilities, Charter of Patient Rights; ethics committees; beginning-of-life issues (MTP, ART, surrogacy, prenatal sex determination); end-of-life issues (euthanasia, advance directives, DNR, withdrawal of life support); organ donation and transplantation; research ethics and informed consent; ethics in psychiatric, paediatric and geriatric care; whistle-blowing; allocation of scarce resources
